basic_information.name: Azure AI Search + Azure OpenAI
basic_information.creator: Microsoft
basic_information.description: Azure AI Search (formerly Azure Cognitive Search) is Microsoft's enterprise-grade cloud search-as-a-service platform that forms the retrieval backbone of the Azure RAG stack. Combined with Azure OpenAI Service, it delivers a turnkey, end-to-end RAG pipeline: document ingestion with integrated chunking and vectorization, hybrid retrieval (keyword + dense vector + semantic ranking), and grounded LLM generation via the 'On Your Data' API or Foundry Agent Service with Foundry IQ. The platform supports agentic retrieval (LLM-driven query decomposition), multimodal search across text and images, and deep integration with the Microsoft ecosystem (SharePoint, OneLake, Azure Blob Storage, Cosmos DB). With 85% of Fortune 500 companies on Azure, it is a dominant choice for enterprises building RAG applications within the Microsoft cloud.
basic_information.release_date: Azure Search originally launched in 2013; renamed Azure Cognitive Search in October 2019; renamed Azure AI Search in November 2023. Vector search and semantic ranker reached GA in November 2023. Agentic retrieval announced May 2025 (preview). Foundry IQ integration late 2025.
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary managed service. Microsoft provides open-source samples at github.com/Azure-Samples (e.g., azure-search-openai-demo with ~6k+ stars, chat-with-your-data-solution-accelerator). Community MCP server at github.com/farzad528/azure-ai-search-mcp-server.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud-managed, distributed search service. Azure AI Search runs as a multi-tenant or dedicated (provisioned) service with configurable Search Units (SUs) composed of partitions (storage) and replicas (query throughput). Supports serverless integrated vectorization (chunking + embedding at indexing time) and both synchronous and asynchronous query patterns. Agentic retrieval adds an LLM-driven query planning layer that decomposes complex queries into parallel subqueries. The 'On Your Data' API (being deprecated in favor of Foundry Agent Service) wraps retrieval and generation into a single endpoint.
technical_architecture.language: Service is cloud-managed (internal implementation not publicly disclosed). SDKs available in Python (azure-search-documents), .NET (Azure.Search.Documents), Java, JavaScript/TypeScript. REST API (OpenAPI spec). Infrastructure-as-code via Azure Resource Manager (ARM), Bicep, Terraform, and Pulumi.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports arbitrary embedding dimensions. Commonly used with: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims, configurable down to 256), text-embedding-3-large (3072 dims, configurable), Azure AI Vision multimodal embeddings (1024 dims). Integrated vectorization supports any Azure OpenAI or Azure AI Services embedding model deployment. Scalar quantization and binary quantization available for compression.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) as primary ANN algorithm, optimized for high-recall, low-latency workloads. Exhaustive KNN (flat/brute-force) also supported for scenarios requiring perfect recall. HNSW parameters are tunable: efConstruction (default 400, range 100-1000), efSearch, and m (number of bi-directional links). Supports scalar quantization (SQ) and binary quantization (BQ) for reduced memory footprint — BQ can reduce vector index size by up to 92.5%. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) for merging hybrid search results.
technical_architecture.scalability: Scales via Search Units (partitions x replicas). Basic tier: up to 3 partitions, 3 replicas, 15 GB storage, 5 indexes. Standard S1: up to 12 partitions x 12 replicas (max 36 SUs), ~300 GB storage per partition. Storage Optimized L1/L2: up to 2 TB per partition. With scalar quantization, certain tiers can support tens of millions of vectors per index. Multi-tenancy supported via index-per-tenant or filters-per-tenant patterns. No cross-region automatic replication (must deploy separate services per region).
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cloud-managed only (Azure). Available in 40+ Azure regions worldwide. No self-hosted or on-premise option. Accessible via Azure Portal, Azure CLI, REST API, SDKs, and Infrastructure-as-Code templates. Private endpoint and VNet injection for network isolation. Azure Government and Azure China (21Vianet) availability for sovereign cloud requirements.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Full-text keyword search (BM25), dense vector search (HNSW/exhaustive KNN), hybrid search (BM25 + vector with RRF fusion), and semantic ranking (Microsoft cross-encoder reranker applied on top of initial results). Agentic retrieval uses an LLM to decompose complex queries into focused subqueries, executes them in parallel, and returns structured, semantically reranked results. Supports pre-filtering and post-filtering on metadata fields alongside vector search.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Integrated chunking via the indexing pipeline: fixed-size chunking (configurable overlap), document-layout-aware chunking using Azure AI Document Intelligence Layout model (semantic chunking by paragraphs, tables, and structural elements). Custom skills via Azure Functions for arbitrary chunking logic. When used with LangChain or LlamaIndex, supports all chunking strategies those frameworks provide (recursive, semantic, markdown-header-based, etc.). The 'Import data (new)' wizard in the Azure Portal automates chunking configuration with no code.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in semantic ranker: Microsoft's proprietary cross-encoder language model that reranks initial BM25 or RRF results based on semantic understanding. Latest model (2025) delivers up to +22 points NDCG@3 improvement when combined with query rewriting, with 2.3x lower latency than previous model. Tested on 90+ datasets across 19 languages. Semantic ranker pricing: Free tier (1,000 queries/month), Standard tier (first 1,000 free, then billed per 1,000 additional queries). Available on Basic tier and above.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Multimodal search GA. Two approaches: (1) Image verbalization — GenAI Prompt skill invokes an LLM during ingestion to create text descriptions of images, which are then vectorized alongside text; (2) Direct multimodal embeddings — uses Azure AI Vision or OpenAI multimodal embedding models to encode images and text into the same vector space. Supports search across text, images, charts, scanned documents, and infographics. Multimodal RAG enables queries like 'show Q1 projections' to retrieve relevant charts and text together.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native built-in GraphRAG. Microsoft's GraphRAG project (github.com/microsoft/graphrag) is a separate open-source library, not directly integrated into Azure AI Search. Azure Cosmos DB with graph capabilities can complement Azure AI Search for knowledge graph workloads. Community discussion suggests combining Azure AI Search for vector/hybrid retrieval with external graph databases for entity-relationship queries, but this requires custom integration.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in citation and source attribution in the 'On Your Data' API (and its successor, Foundry Agent Service with Foundry IQ). Responses include citations linking claims back to specific source documents with file name, title, and URL. Foundry IQ provides grounded answers from enterprise data (SharePoint, OneLake, ADLS, web) without custom RAG code. Content field and title field are used for citation display. Note: 'On Your Data' is deprecated (retirement tied to GPT-4o model retirement, approximately June-October 2026); migration to Foundry Agent Service recommended.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Agentic retrieval handles context optimization by decomposing complex queries into subqueries and aggregating only the most relevant chunks. Configurable 'strictness' parameter in 'On Your Data' controls the threshold for filtering out irrelevant chunks. Configurable number of document chunks returned per query. Semantic ranker promotes most relevant content to the top of results. Query rewriting (generative query rewriting) improves retrieval precision. No built-in summarization or compression — relies on the LLM's context window capacity and the quality of retrieved chunks.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Typical vector search query latency is under 500ms for well-optimized indexes using HNSW. Latest semantic ranker model offers up to 2.3x lower latency than its predecessor. Agentic retrieval adds additional latency due to LLM-driven query planning. End-to-end RAG latency depends on the generation model (Azure OpenAI GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, etc.). HNSW parameters (efSearch, efConstruction) are tunable to trade off latency vs. recall. Binary quantization provides the best speed improvement among compression options. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Not publicly benchmarked as a single metric. Throughput scales with replicas (add replicas for higher QPS). Microsoft provides a performance benchmarking guide recommending custom load testing. Standard S1 with 1 replica handles moderate query loads; production deployments typically use 2-3+ replicas. Indexing throughput depends on tier and document complexity. No official QPS numbers published. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Semantic ranker delivers up to +22 points NDCG@3 improvement over baseline BM25/RRF when combined with query rewriting, tested on 90+ datasets across 19 languages. Hybrid search (BM25 + vector + semantic ranking) consistently outperforms pure vector search on enterprise retrieval benchmarks. Internal Microsoft benchmarks use NDCG@3 and NDCG@10 (aligned with BEIR/MIRACL). Agentic retrieval claims up to 40% better relevance for complex queries compared to classic single-query RAG.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: No standardized public ANN-Benchmark submission for Azure AI Search specifically. Microsoft publishes internal results: hybrid retrieval + semantic ranking outperforms vector-only search across multiple datasets; new semantic ranker model (2025) tested on 90+ datasets including BEIR and MIRACL benchmarks. Embedding model performance depends on the chosen model (OpenAI text-embedding-3 models have their own MTEB rankings). Microsoft recommends custom benchmarking with Azure AI Foundry RAG evaluators (faithfulness, groundedness, relevance, coherence). [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Native integrations with LangChain (Python: AzureAISearchRetriever, AzureAISearchVectorStore; JS: @langchain/azure-search), LlamaIndex (AzureAISearchVectorStore, AzureCognitiveSearchReader), and Haystack. Compatible with Semantic Kernel (Microsoft's orchestration SDK). Works with DSPy for programmatic prompt optimization. Terraform, Bicep, ARM templates, and Pulumi for infrastructure-as-code. Azure SDK for Python, .NET, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Azure OpenAI Service: GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.5-preview, o1, o3-mini, and other OpenAI models. Embedding models: text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large, text-embedding-ada-002. Azure AI Vision for multimodal embeddings. Via Foundry Model Catalog: Meta Llama, Mistral, Phi-3/Phi-4, Cohere, and 1,600+ models. Custom models can be used via integrated vectorization with custom Azure OpenAI or Azure AI Services deployments.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Community MCP server available (farzad528/azure-ai-search-mcp-server on GitHub). Azure Samples demonstrate MCP integration with both LangChain.js and LlamaIndex.TS (azure-ai-travel-agents sample). Foundry Agent Service supports MCP and A2A protocols. No official first-party Azure AI Search MCP server from Microsoft yet, but the ecosystem is converging on MCP support.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Built-in indexers for: Azure Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Azure Table Storage, Azure Files, Azure Cosmos DB (SQL API, MongoDB API, Gremlin API), Azure SQL Database, SQL Server on Azure VMs, Microsoft OneLake (Fabric), SharePoint in Microsoft 365. Third-party connectors via partner ecosystem. Custom data ingestion via Push API (REST) or SDK. Web crawler not built-in (available via Azure AI Document Intelligence or custom implementation). The 'Import data (new)' portal wizard supports Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2, and OneLake.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Azure Monitor and Azure Log Analytics for service-level metrics (query latency, throttling, indexing rates). Application Insights for end-to-end request tracing. Azure Diagnostic Logs for detailed query and indexing logs. Compatible with OpenTelemetry via Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry SDK. When used within LangChain or LlamaIndex pipelines, compatible with LangSmith, Langfuse, and Arize Phoenix for LLM-level tracing. No built-in RAG-specific observability dashboard — relies on Azure Monitor + third-party tools.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Provisioned (always-on) pricing billed per Search Unit (SU) per hour/month. A Search Unit = 1 partition x 1 replica. Pricing varies by tier: Free, Basic, Standard (S1, S2, S3), and Storage Optimized (L1, L2). Semantic ranker billed separately per 1,000 queries (free tier: 1,000/month; standard: first 1,000 free, then per-1,000 increments). Azure OpenAI costs billed separately per token (input/output). No per-query or per-vector pricing for core search — only provisioned capacity.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Free tier available: 1 service per subscription, 50 MB storage, 3 indexes, no SLA. Limited to shared resources. Semantic ranker free plan: 1,000 queries/month. Azure OpenAI has separate free trial credits for new accounts. Free tier suitable for development and small POCs only.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Basic tier: ~$75/month per SU (2 GB storage, 15 indexes). Standard S1: ~$245/month per SU (25 GB per partition). Standard S2: ~$980/month per SU (100 GB per partition). Standard S3: ~$1,960/month per SU (200 GB per partition). Storage Optimized L1: ~$1,000/month per SU (1 TB per partition). Storage Optimized L2: ~$2,000/month per SU (2 TB per partition). For 1M documents at S1 with 3 partitions + 2 replicas (6 SUs): ~$1,470/month for search alone, plus Azure OpenAI embedding + generation costs. Semantic ranker adds per-query costs at scale. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Full TCO includes: (1) Azure AI Search service (always-on, provisioned SUs — minimum ~$75/month for Basic), (2) Azure OpenAI embedding costs for vectorization (~$0.02/1M tokens for text-embedding-3-small), (3) Azure OpenAI generation costs ($2.50-$10/1M input tokens depending on model), (4) Semantic ranker query fees, (5) Azure Blob Storage or other data source storage, (6) Azure AI Document Intelligence for advanced document parsing ($1.50-$15/1K pages depending on model), (7) Networking (private endpoints, VNet), (8) Azure Monitor for observability. Key cost driver: the always-on provisioned nature means you pay even during idle periods, unlike serverless alternatives. Minimum production deployment (Basic + Azure OpenAI): ~$150-300/month. Enterprise deployment (S1 multi-replica + semantic ranker + GPT-4o): $2,000-5,000+/month.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in enterprise search and RAG for Microsoft-ecosystem organizations. Azure holds 25% of the global cloud infrastructure market (second to AWS). 85% of Fortune 500 companies use Azure. Azure AI services grew 42% in 2025, with the AI revenue run rate hitting $13 billion (175% YoY growth). Azure AI Search is a strategic component of Microsoft's AI platform (Azure AI Foundry, Copilot, Foundry Agent Service). Dominant position among enterprises using Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Air India (customer service AI), H&R Block (tax Q&A), Volvo (invoice/claims processing), DocuSign, JATO Dynamics, Kinectify, Medigold Health, and thousands of enterprise customers via Microsoft Azure. Microsoft Copilot products (Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot) use Azure AI Search internally. Over 53,000 Azure AI customers total (one-third joined in the past 12 months).
adoption_and_market.community_size: No dedicated open-source community (proprietary service). Large Azure developer ecosystem: Microsoft Learn documentation, Microsoft Tech Community blog, Microsoft Q&A forums, Stack Overflow tag (azure-cognitive-search / azure-ai-search). GitHub samples: azure-search-openai-demo (~6k+ stars), numerous Azure-Samples repositories. Azure MVP community. Annual Microsoft Build and Ignite conferences feature Azure AI Search sessions.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: N/A — Azure AI Search is a product of Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT, ~$3T market cap). Azure surpassed $75 billion in revenue in FY 2025 (up 34%). Microsoft has invested over $108 billion in cloud infrastructure including 60+ AI data centers globally. Azure AI is a strategic priority with massive capital allocation.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (AWS RAG stack, serverless, multi-vector-store backends), Google Vertex AI Search (Google Cloud RAG, strong Gemini integration). Vector database competitors: Pinecone (purpose-built, low-latency), Weaviate (open-source, multi-modal), Qdrant (high-performance, Rust-based), Milvus/Zilliz (scalable, open-source), Elasticsearch (established, hybrid search). Key Azure AI Search differentiators: (1) deepest Microsoft ecosystem integration (SharePoint, OneLake, Microsoft 365 Copilot), (2) built-in semantic ranker (no separate reranker needed), (3) integrated vectorization (no external embedding pipeline), (4) agentic retrieval for complex queries, (5) enterprise compliance (ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, FedRAMP). Key weaknesses: always-on provisioned pricing (no serverless option for search), no self-hosted deployment, vendor lock-in to Azure.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best suited for startups already invested in the Microsoft/Azure ecosystem, or those targeting enterprise customers who require Microsoft compliance certifications. Ideal for teams of 3-15 engineers building B2B SaaS with document search, knowledge management, or customer support RAG. Strong fit for: (1) enterprise SaaS products where customers mandate Azure compliance, (2) products integrating with Microsoft 365 (SharePoint, OneLake), (3) teams needing built-in semantic ranking without managing separate reranker infrastructure. Less ideal for: bootstrapped startups seeking minimal cost (always-on pricing starts at ~$75/month even for Basic), teams preferring multi-cloud or open-source flexibility, consumer applications with unpredictable traffic patterns (no serverless option), or startups where AWS is the primary cloud. Consider the free tier for POCs but plan for Basic or S1 for production.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Buy (use Azure AI Search) when: your stack is already on Azure, enterprise customers require Microsoft compliance, you need integrated vectorization and semantic ranking out of the box, team lacks vector DB expertise, or you need SharePoint/OneLake integration. Build (self-host alternatives) when: cost sensitivity is paramount (Qdrant/Milvus self-hosted can be cheaper), you need multi-cloud portability, you require fine-grained control over indexing algorithms, or you want a serverless pay-per-query model (consider Pinecone Serverless). Hybrid approach: use Azure AI Search for retrieval but manage your own generation pipeline with LangChain/LlamaIndex for maximum flexibility over prompts and LLM selection.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC in 1-2 days using the 'Import data (new)' wizard in Azure Portal (fully no-code: connect data source, configure chunking, deploy). Production deployment in 2-4 weeks including index optimization, semantic ranker tuning, security configuration (private endpoints, RBAC), and integration testing. Enterprise deployments with SharePoint connectors, custom skills, and agentic retrieval: 4-8 weeks. The Azure-Search-OpenAI-Demo accelerator (GitHub) provides a production-ready reference architecture that can be deployed in under a day.
key_lessons: Start with the 'Import data (new)' portal wizard for rapid POCs — it handles chunking, vectorization, and index creation with zero code. But move to Infrastructure-as-Code (Bicep/Terraform) for production to ensure reproducibility and environment parity.

Always enable hybrid search (BM25 + vector) with semantic ranking — Microsoft's own benchmarks show this combination consistently outperforms pure vector search. The semantic ranker is the single most impactful feature for retrieval quality.

Budget for always-on costs: unlike serverless vector databases, Azure AI Search charges per Search Unit continuously. A Basic tier at ~$75/month is the minimum for production. Factor in Azure OpenAI token costs separately — generation costs often exceed search infrastructure costs.

Plan the 'On Your Data' to Foundry Agent Service migration now: the On Your Data API is deprecated (retirement ~June-October 2026). Foundry IQ in Foundry Agent Service is the successor, offering improved grounding without custom RAG code. Starting with Foundry Agent Service avoids migration debt.

Leverage Azure AI Document Intelligence for advanced document parsing — it provides layout-aware, semantic chunking that is dramatically better than naive fixed-size splitting for PDFs, scanned documents, and table-heavy content. It is a differentiating advantage of the Azure RAG stack.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes. Azure Portal provides the 'Import data (new)' wizard (formerly 'Import and vectorize data') for no-code RAG setup: connect to Azure Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2, or OneLake, configure chunking and vectorization, create and populate an index, and test queries — all via a guided UI. Also supports the 'Import data' wizard for keyword-only indexes. Azure AI Foundry (formerly Azure AI Studio) provides additional visual tools for building RAG applications with evaluation capabilities.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy with managed AI services, CRISP-DM applied to RAG) and Session 4 (AI business models & strategy — Azure cloud economics, enterprise scaling considerations)

confidence.data_quality: High — based on official Microsoft Learn documentation, Microsoft Tech Community blog posts, Azure pricing pages, and corroborated by third-party analyses (ITmagination, Pondhouse Data, InfoQ, DEV Community, ITNEXT).
confidence.cross_reference: Microsoft Learn (learn.microsoft.com/azure/search), Microsoft Tech Community Blog (techcommunity.microsoft.com), Azure pricing page (azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/search), Pondhouse Data RAG tutorial, ITmagination Azure AI Search guide, InfoQ agentic retrieval coverage, DEV Community vector search articles, GitHub Azure-Samples repositories.
confidence.caveats: Exact pricing varies by region and may change — figures cited are approximate US East rates. The 'On Your Data' API is deprecated and approaching retirement (June-October 2026); Foundry Agent Service with Foundry IQ is the recommended successor. Agentic retrieval is in preview (2025-11-01-preview API) and may evolve before GA. Performance benchmarks are not published on standardized third-party platforms (e.g., ANN-Benchmarks) — Microsoft publishes internal results. The service evolves rapidly (multimodal search, agentic retrieval, Foundry IQ) so some details may become outdated. No serverless pricing option exists — the always-on provisioned model can be costly for low-traffic workloads.
confidence.security_posture: Enterprise-grade security: encryption at rest (Microsoft-managed or customer-managed keys via Azure Key Vault), encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), optional double encryption. Network security: IP firewall rules, private endpoints, VNet injection, network security perimeter. Authentication: API keys (admin + query) and Azure RBAC via Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). Compliance: ISO 27001, ISO 27018, SOC 1/2/3, FedRAMP Moderate (Azure Government), HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS. Data residency controls by Azure region selection. Known attack surfaces: prompt injection via poisoned indexed documents, embedding inversion risks with stored vectors. Mitigations: Azure AI Content Safety, Responsible AI practices, Entra ID-based access control, private endpoint network isolation.
